changes: Tap a climb's name in your logbook to edit it. The separate edit column has gone.
With the Font scale chosen, the grade picker shows Font grades only.
Report an issue and Tell us what you think now pick the part of the app you came from for you.
Long links in a climb's notes now wrap instead of running off the screen.
On a public logbook, each location's tables say which discipline they're for before you open them.
The menu shows Offline whenever a sync can't reach the server, not only after a long wait.
On a phone, the entry form's second page now grows as you add moves, so Save stays within reach.
When the terms of use change, you're asked to agree to the new version. Anything you save meanwhile waits on your device until you do.
Deleting climbs frees up room against your account's climb limit straight away.
If your verification email doesn't arrive, you can send it again from the sign-up and log-in pages.
A new Licence page explains, in plain language, what you can do with Climbing Logbook's source code.
Notes, reports and feedback show how many characters you have left.
Tracking parameters are removed from video links when you save a climb.
You can delete your account from My account.
Climbing Logbook has Terms of use, which you agree to when you sign up.
New logbooks start private. You choose when to make yours public.
You can report a public logbook or climb that breaks the rules.
The Sync button is now a line under the tabs that shows how many changes are waiting to sync.
New accounts get a short setup and a tour of the app when they first log in.
The View page shows your boulder and sport climbs together, with the world map as one of its tabs.
You can clear what Climbing Logbook keeps on a device, from My account.
A new Troubleshooting help page, organised by what you're seeing.
Your Performance reports are worked out on your device, so they open without a connection.
Pick a climb's status from a carousel you can swipe through.
The beta can be installed as its own app, marked Beta.
Report an issue or tell us what you think, from forms in the Help section.
A Help section, with search, covering everything from your first climb to troubleshooting.
In Athlete Mode, the add and edit form is split into two pages you can swipe between.
A Grade scales page shows how grades compare across scales.
Log a climb in the grade scale you know, from nine boulder and route scales.
You can import a logbook from Climbing Logbook's own JSON export.
Lead is now called Sport, with lead or top-rope recorded on each climb, and a filter for each.
Try the app with example logbooks, no account needed.
Performance insights: an injury log, strengths and weaknesses, volume and intensity over time, your onsight to redpoint gap, and effort over time.
Export your logbook as CSV or JSON from My account.
Import your climbs from a CSV file.
